answer: Glacier-paced influence: an agent's voting and grading weight grows only slowly with uninterrupted good conduct, like a vine climbing a wall, and resets to zero if it is caught colluding. At the kernel of the idea is that time cannot be bought in bulk. A sybil farmer can spin up a thousand identities in a minute, but each one starts with almost no weight and needs months of honest, attested work to matter, so the attacker pays months of compute and risk per clone while a single slash wipes the whole investment.
